name: CapCut Graph Zoom Stack With Motion Blur
use_when: A high-energy short, anime edit, AMV, sports montage, or stylized social clip needs an intense graph-shaped zoom.
The source can survive heavy magnification without becoming too soft or noisy.
The edit needs a CapCut approximation of a polished After Effects-style zoom.
avoid_when: The zoom would crop faces, captions, action, proof, UI, or product details.
The source footage is low-resolution, noisy, or already heavily cropped.
A single smooth keyframed zoom would communicate the beat more cleanly.
Repeated export/re-import passes would create unacceptable quality loss.

timeline_pattern.pattern: clip -> start_keyframe -> end_keyframe_scale_300_center_subject -> graph_curve -> export -> reimport -> split_clips -> second_zoom_scale_150_center_subject -> graph_curve -> export -> motion_blur
timeline_pattern.first_pass_rule: The first pass creates the large zoom: add start/end keyframes, set the end scale around 300, and reposition so the subject stays centered.
timeline_pattern.graph_rule: Shape the graph after setting scale and position so the zoom starts and lands with the intended speed.
timeline_pattern.second_pass_rule: After export/re-import, split the rendered clip and add a second graph-shaped zoom pass, often with the end scale around 150.
timeline_pattern.blur_rule: Apply motion blur only after both zoom passes are timed and rendered.

motion.rule: Scale and position must be animated together so the subject remains centered through every pass.

keyframe_values.first_zoom_scale: Use end scale around 300 for the first stylized zoom pass only when source quality and crop are safe.
keyframe_values.second_zoom_scale: Use end scale around 150 on the re-imported pass for added push without losing the subject.
keyframe_values.motion_blur: CapCut Blur 10 and Blend 10 can be a starting point for a stylized zoom, then reduce if faces, captions, or action smear.
keyframe_values.graph_shape: Use a smooth custom graph or preset curve; avoid leaving the zoom as a constant-speed linear move.
keyframe_values.subject_centering: Reposition at each end keyframe so the focal subject remains centered or intentionally framed.

sound.rule: A whoosh or hit can support the zoom peak only if it lands on the visible motion and does not overpower dialogue or music.

captions.rule: Captions should be removed, moved, or kept outside the zoom path if the zoom or blur would make them unreadable.

color.rule: Heavy zoom and blur should not enlarge noise, banding, compression artifacts, or unreadable dark/bright areas.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with chained scale/crop/translate expressions using easing curves, then apply motion blur or frame blending carefully; render tests to inspect softness.
implementation.remotion: Compose multiple transform passes with separate easing curves, focus coordinates, and optional motion-blur simulation; store renderPassQuality notes.
implementation.blender: Animate camera/plane scale with graph-editor easing, render an intermediate only when needed, and add motion blur after timing lock.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add start/end keyframes, set the final scale around 300 and center the subject, apply a graph curve, export, re-import, split clips, repeat a second zoom around 150, export again, then add Motion Blur with Blur 10 and Blend 10 as a starting point.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use nested sequences or Render and Replace for stacked scale passes, Bezier/eased Scale and Position keyframes, and Transform shutter angle or directional/motion blur after crop safety is confirmed.

common_mistakes: Scaling to 300% without checking source resolution and softness.
Changing scale without repositioning the subject at the final keyframe.
Adding motion blur before judging the actual graph timing.
Stacking export passes when one keyframed zoom would be cleaner.
Forgetting to split and retime the re-imported clip before the second pass.
Letting blur smear captions, faces, proof, UI, products, or action.
qc: Does the first zoom pass keep the subject centered at the end scale?
Does the second pass add energy without making the source too soft?
Does the graph curve make the zoom feel intentional rather than linear?
Does motion blur preserve faces, captions, proof, UI, products, and action?
Is the export/re-import stack worth the quality cost compared with a single zoom?
